content.title: About
content.content: Cereal, K's, plain is a dry whole‑grain cereal designed for quick breakfast preparation. The flakes have a neutral taste, making them a versatile base for fruit, nuts, milk or yogurt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cereal, K's, plain is made from whole wheat grains enriched with vitamins and minerals.
The flakes contain low amounts of sugar, suitable for reduced‑sugar diets.
The product is often used as a base for homemade granola bars and desserts.
Packaging is typically recyclable, reducing environmental impact.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: The cereal provides sustained energy through slowly digestible carbs.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Enrichment with vitamins B1, B2 and B6 supports metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron contributes to hemoglobin formation and helps maintain energy levels.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Low saturated fat content makes the cereal suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains wheat, so it is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: When sweetened with dried fruit or syrups, the overall sugar level can increase.

items.title: Potential additives
items.content: Some versions may contain artificial flavors; check the label if you are sensitive to additives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour hot or cold milk over the flakes, add fresh fruit, berries, nuts or honey to taste. They can also be used in baking, as a base for granola, or blended into smoothies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. After opening, use within 4‑6 weeks to maintain crispness.

fruit-smoothie-juice-drink-with-dairy.title: Fruit Smoothie Juice Drink with Dairy

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit smoothie juice drink with dairy is a ready‑to‑drink beverage that blends fruit purees, juices, and dairy components. It combines the sweetness of ripe fruits with a creamy milk texture, delivering a pleasant taste and nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Smoothies are often made from several fruit varieties, boosting their vitamin profile.
Adding dairy makes the drink richer in protein and calcium compared with pure fruit juices.
The beverage is conveniently packaged in a sealed bottle that stays fresh for up to 24 hours without refrigeration.
Some versions contain a small amount of added sugar for flavor balance, but sugar‑free options are also available.
In many countries these drinks are sold as “ready‑to‑drink” (RTD) and are subject to specific food regulations.

items.title: Rich in vitamins C and A
items.content: The fruit component supplies vitamin C for immune support and vitamin A for eye and skin health.

items.title: Source of calcium and protein
items.content: Dairy provides calcium for bones and protein that aids tissue repair.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: Water from the juices and milk helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Fruit polyphenols and vitamin E from dairy act as antioxidants, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Simple sugars from fruit combined with dairy protein give a quick and sustained energy source.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who cannot digest lactose may experience bloating, gas, or diarrhea.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk proteins (casein, whey) can have allergic reactions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Some versions contain added sugar, which is undesirable for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Acidic fruit juices may aggravate heartburn in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Consume the drink chilled straight from the bottle after opening. It can be used as a base for cocktails, added to dessert sauces, or enjoyed as a refreshing snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2 °C–6 °C. Once opened, finish within 24 hours. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.

content.title: About
content.content: Lettuce is a leafy vegetable commonly used as a fresh topping for sandwiches, salads, and other dishes. It has a crisp texture, mild flavor, and a slightly bitter note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: There are over 100 varieties of lettuce, including romaine, iceberg, butterhead, and leaf lettuce.
Lettuce is composed of more than 95% water, making it an excellent source of hydration.
Lettuce leaves can absorb light but perform photosynthesis less efficiently than many other plants.
Beyond raw consumption, lettuce is sometimes lightly sautéed or steamed in culinary applications.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Lettuce provides a good amount of vitamin K, which is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and folate
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, while folate is important for cell division and fetal development during pregnancy.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Lettuce is very low in calories, making it helpful for weight management.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Leafy greens contain carotenoids and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in lettuce promotes regular bowel movements and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Lettuce can be contaminated with bacteria such as E. coli, so thorough washing before consumption is important.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Conventional lettuce may contain pesticide residues; choosing organic or washing well reduces the risk.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to leafy vegetables, resulting in itching or swelling.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lettuce is typically eaten raw: added to sandwiches, salads, wraps, and smoothies. It can also be lightly sautéed, steamed, or incorporated into warm dishes while retaining its crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store lettuce in the refrigerator in an airtight container or bag with a small amount of moisture. Use within 3–5 days. Discard if leaves turn yellow or develop an off odor.

content.title: About
content.content: The ostrich is a large, flightless bird native to Africa. Ostrich meat is considered a lean, high‑protein option with a mild, slightly sweet flavor that resembles beef.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ostriches can reach heights of up to 2.7 m and weigh over 150 kg.
Ostrich eggs are the largest of any bird; one egg weighs about 1.4 kg.
In the wild, ostriches can run up to 70 km/h.
Ostrich meat contains less fat than beef and almost twice as much iron.
Ostriches are farmed not only for meat but also for feathers, leather, and eggs.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ostrich meat provides about 22 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with beef, ostrich meat contains only 2–3 % fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: High iron content
items.content: The iron in ostrich meat is highly bioavailable and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Source of zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals support immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low cholesterol
items.content: Ostrich meat has lower cholesterol levels than most red meats.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to ostrich meat.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Like any raw meat, ostrich can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; proper cooking is essential.

items.title: Higher cost
items.content: Ostrich meat is typically more expensive than conventional meats, which may limit frequent consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ostrich meat can be prepared like beef: pan‑seared, roasted, stewed, or grilled. It pairs well with herbs, spices, wine‑based or tomato sauces. Fillets are often sliced into thin steaks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh ostrich meat in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: A butterscotch or caramel topping is a thick sweet sauce made from sugar, butter, cream and flavorings. It is used to drizzle over ice cream, desserts, pancakes, waffles and drinks, giving them a rich buttery‑caramel taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “butterscotch” comes from butter and scotch, though the product has no connection to Scotland.
Caramel toppings often contain sea salt, which enhances sweetness through flavor contrast.
In the United States the topping is frequently served as a soft‑serve sauce that stays pourable at low temperatures.
Traditional recipes caramelize sugar before adding butter and cream to achieve a smooth texture.
Vegan versions exist, replacing dairy butter and cream with plant‑based alternatives.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sugar and fats provide quick calories, which can be useful during high energy demand.

items.title: Contains vitamin A
items.content: Butter contributes a modest amount of vitamin A, important for vision and immunity.

items.title: Mood enhancer
items.content: Sweet taste stimulates serotonin production, helping improve mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may raise blood glucose levels and contribute to tooth decay.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Large amounts of butter increase saturated fat intake, which can affect cardiovascular health.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should choose vegan alternatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drizzle over ice cream, add to coffee, cocktails, pancakes, waffles, yogurt, or use as a filling for cupcakes. Warm gently for a thinner consistency if needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator in an airtight jar for up to 2 weeks. Warm before use, but avoid boiling to preserve flavor.
